lead.claim: Exoskeleton training improves upper limb motor function in stroke patients.
lead.context: Why this matters: This systematic review looked at how exoskeleton-assisted training compares to conventional rehabilitation for upper limb function after stroke.

supporting.claim: Virtual reality or aerobic exercise can be added to MS rehab.
supporting.context: Why this matters: This study investigated if adding virtual reality or aerobic exercise to conventional rehabilitation was superior for patients with Multiple Sclerosis.

supporting.claim: Regular exercise can promote stem cell production and mobilization.
supporting.context: Why this matters: This systematic review explored the relationship between physical activity and stem cell production across different age groups.

supporting.claim: Long spinal fusion might impact movement tasks years later.
supporting.context: Why this matters: This observational study examined movement quality in women with scoliosis after surgical and non-surgical treatment.

supporting.claim: Post-ACLR, operated limb strength determines jump performance.
supporting.context: Why this matters: This study investigated the relationship between isometric strength, inter-limb differences, and jump performance after ACL reconstruction.
